inventory.note: Django backend, organization_management/apps/*; recent commits (git log -20) are all frontend (SPA) work — no recent backend commits, so the sample was chosen from apps/statuses per the documented status-transition invariants in obsidian-vault/Personnel-Records/Decisions.md, plus a repo-wide grep of I/O boundaries (Celery tasks, admin.py, document/notify services).
Canonical contract for apps/statuses invariants used to check current code.

Not present in .venv (pip show ruff -> not found). Installed via `./.venv/bin/pip install ruff -q` for this audit run, then `./.venv/bin/python -m ruff check . --statistics` executed from Backend/PersonnelStatus/Personnel-Records. Result: 1518 total violations, 397 auto-fixable. No ruff.toml/pyproject ruff config found outside .venv, so this run used ruff's built-in defaults, not a project-pinned rule set.

findings.title: complete_expired_statuses lacks the per-employee transaction isolation that apply_planned_statuses explicitly added for the same invariant

evidence.detail: complete_expired_statuses (line 559) is wrapped in ONE outer @transaction.atomic covering the whole loop over all expired statuses. Inside the loop it calls self.create_status(...) (line 586-590) for every non-IN_SERVICE expired status, and create_status is itself @transaction.atomic (services.py line 27) with no try/except around it here. By contrast, apply_planned_statuses (line 478-557, same file) explicitly wraps EACH row in its own `with transaction.atomic():` block plus a per-row try/except ValidationError (lines 513-553), and its own docstring (lines 482-486, 508-512) states the reason: 'задача ежедневная и массовая, и один сотрудник с противоречивыми данными не должен оставлять без статусов всех остальных.' complete_expired_statuses has no equivalent per-row isolation or exception handling, so a ValidationError raised by create_status for one employee (e.g. full_clean() rejecting an edge-case date collision, per the documented clean()-overlap ITfootguns in Decisions.md) propagates out of the single outer atomic block and rolls back status completions for every OTHER employee processed earlier in the same call, silently reverting work that had already succeeded.

recommendation.text: Give complete_expired_statuses the same per-row `with transaction.atomic(): ... except ValidationError: continue` pattern already used in apply_planned_statuses, so one bad row cannot roll back the whole batch.

findings.title: Celery status-lifecycle tasks catch all exceptions and return an unread {'success': False} dict instead of failing/retrying — batch failures are invisible

evidence.detail: Both @shared_task entry points (apply_planned_statuses_task lines 15-47, complete_expired_statuses_task lines 50-82) wrap the entire service call in `except Exception as e: logger.error(...); return {'success': False, 'error': str(e)}`. Neither task is declared with `bind=True`/`autoretry_for`/`retry_kwargs`, and callers invoke them via Celery beat (fire-and-forget `.delay()`), so nothing ever inspects the returned dict. Combined with RAW-00000001, a single bad row can make complete_expired_statuses_task silently report a Celery-level SUCCESS while zero statuses were actually completed for that run, with no retry and no alert — this is the exact mechanism behind the already-documented Known-Issue 'Celery-задачи статусов не доезжают на стенде' (obsidian-vault/Personnel-Records/Known-Issues.md), except this finding is about production-mode silent failure, not the stand's broker being unreachable.

recommendation.text: Either let the exception propagate (Celery marks the task FAILED, visible in monitoring/Flower) or add autoretry_for + an alert on repeated failure; a swallowed exception encoded only in a discarded return value is operationally equivalent to no error handling.

findings.title: Bare `except:` clauses swallow all exceptions (including unrelated bugs) around employee/staff_unit lookups in JWT claims and admin display

evidence.detail: `./.venv/bin/python -m ruff check . --statistics` from Backend/PersonnelStatus/Personnel-Records reports exactly 3 E722 (bare-except) violations project-wide. Confirmed by source read at jwt_serializers.py:56 and :134 (both `except: pass` guarding `hasattr(user.employee, 'staff_unit')`) and common/admin.py:338 (`except: pass` guarding the same pattern in EffectiveDivisionDisplay). All three swallow every exception type, not just the DoesNotExist/AttributeError the code is defending against, so an unrelated bug in that code path (e.g. a broken property) would silently disappear into a token claim or admin label instead of surfacing.

recommendation.text: Narrow to `except (Employee.staff_unit.RelatedObjectDoesNotExist, AttributeError): pass` (or ruff-suggested `except Exception:`), matching the pattern already used correctly elsewhere in the same files' 40 BLE001 blind-except findings.

findings.title: ruff check reports 1518 violations project-wide; no project ruff config found

evidence.detail: ruff was NOT installed in .venv (`./.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .` -> 'No module named ruff'; `pip show ruff` -> not found). Installed it for this audit (`./.venv/bin/pip install ruff -q`) and ran `./.venv/bin/python -m ruff check . --statistics` from Backend/PersonnelStatus/Personnel-Records. Result: 1518 total errors (397 auto-fixable, 71 more with --unsafe-fixes). Top categories: RUF012 mutable-class-default (418), F811 redefined-while-unused (372), I001 unsorted-imports (179), EXE002 shebang-missing-executable-file (151), SIM117 (55), F401 unused-import (52), RUF059 unused-unpacked-variable (48), BLE001 blind-except (40), S110 try-except-pass (13), E722 bare-except (3). No ruff.toml or pyproject.toml with a [tool.ruff] section was found outside .venv, so this is ruff's default rule set, not a project-curated gate — the count is a raw baseline, not evidence the project intends to enforce all these categories.

recommendation.text: If ruff is meant to be the lint gate, commit a pinned ruff config (requirements + pyproject.toml [tool.ruff]) selecting the rule set actually intended (CLAUDE.md elsewhere records 'ruff check (E,F)' as the intended gate for a sibling project) — running bare defaults surfaces 1518 mostly-stylistic findings that drown out the handful of real issues (BLE001, S110, E722).

findings.title: operations app does not import core.models — isolation guard holds (no violation found)

evidence.detail: `grep -rn "from.*core.*import.*models\|from.*core import models\|core\.models\." organization_management/apps/operations --include=*.py` (excluding tests) returned zero matches. No test file named test_isolation.py or equivalent exists anywhere under organization_management (grep for test_isolation/test_admin_platform/operations_does_not_import_core_models found nothing) — the tested guard `apps/operations/tests/test_isolation.py` referenced in memory feedback_vaps_arch_guards.md does not exist in this codebase (that memory describes the removed donor repo Backend/VAPS, per obsidian-vault Decisions.md 'Переезд core...'). So the isolation property currently holds by inspection, but it is UNGUARDED — nothing would catch a future regression.

recommendation.text: No fix needed today; if the operations/core isolation matters going forward, port a lightweight AST-based test (grep-in-CI or an import-linter rule) into Personnel-Records rather than relying on the memory of a guard that lived in the deleted donor repo.

findings.title: Django Admin registers transactional/business models (Employee, EmployeeStatus, StatusChangeHistory, StatusDocument, SecondmentRequest, EmployeeTransferHistory), not just reference dictionaries, with no guard test enforcing catalogs-only

evidence.detail: CLAUDE.md/project memory (feedback_vaps_arch_guards.md) documents the architectural rule 'Admin=только справочники' (Django Admin should register only reference/dictionary models, business models are service-only-write). Grepping every apps/*/admin.py for admin.site.register/@admin.register shows: dictionaries/admin.py (Position, Rank) and divisions/admin.py (Division) are legitimate catalogs, but employees/admin.py registers Employee (@admin.register, line 25) and EmployeeTransferHistory (line 130) — both transactional personnel records; statuses/admin.py registers EmployeeStatus (line 32), StatusChangeHistory (line 178), StatusDocument (line 220) — the exact models whose lifecycle is governed by the invariant-heavy StatusApplicationService documented in Decisions.md (single-active-status, full_clean() side effects, ordering-sensitive close/cancel logic); secondments/admin.py does a bare `admin.site.register(SecondmentRequest)` with NO custom ModelAdmin at all, giving raw CRUD on a model whose `status` field (secondments/models.py, ApprovalStatus choices) is otherwise only meant to change via `secondments/api/views.py::approve`, which per Decisions.md ('Один активный статус на сотрудника') creates the paired EmployeeStatus SECONDED_TO record through the service layer. Because SecondmentRequest.status is a plain CharField with no save()-time enforcement tying it to EmployeeStatus, an admin user can flip status to 'approved' directly in Django Admin without ever creating the corresponding EmployeeStatus — leaving the invariant 'approved secondment => exactly one SECONDED_TO status record' silently broken, with no error raised anywhere. No test file matching test_admin*catalog*/test_admin_registry* exists in this codebase to catch such registrations (grep across organization_management found none), unlike the guard the project memory describes for the (now-removed) donor repo.

recommendation.text: Either unregister SecondmentRequest/EmployeeStatus/StatusChangeHistory/StatusDocument/EmployeeTransferHistory from Django Admin (route all writes through StatusApplicationService / the secondments approve() flow), or make them read-only ModelAdmins, and add a guard test enumerating admin.site._registry against an explicit dictionary-model allowlist so a future PR can't silently reintroduce a transactional-model registration.

findings.title: No measured scalability baseline found for Personnel-Records in docs/ or obsidian-vault/

evidence.detail: Searched obsidian-vault/Personnel-Records/{Status,Decisions,Known-Issues}.md for a load-test result or a documented row-count-where-it-got-slow. Found N+1/query-shape gotchas (MPTT + values().annotate() without order_by(), Prefetch to_attr requirements) described as correctness/perf traps, but no measured throughput/latency baseline or a row count at which anything degraded. Per the audit instructions, this is reported as insufficient rather than fabricated.

recommendation.text: No scalability-limit finding can be made without a real measurement; if this matters for the release gate, run a load test against a realistic row count (the vault records ~14 employees on the dev stand, which is far below anything that would surface a scalability limit) before claiming a number.
